text:
maria: FYI — us-west-2 queue depth for redwood-1-large-v2 jumped hard around 09:12 UTC. current depth ~12,300, GPU util ~97%, admission drop rate 35%. p50=180ms p95=1.6s. seeing a few OOMs in logs. graph: https://grafana/redwood/d/queues/usw2
aj: saw the same. looks like a mix of long sequences and a traffic surge from a top customer. per-model breakdown shows redwood-1-large-v2 and a smaller spike on compatible-llm-medium.
simon: is backpressure layer tripping? what are admission control thresholds right now?
maria: admission policy for that pool is 'max_inflight_per_gpu=48, pool_capacity=120g' (gpu-equivalent). backpressure metrics show we started shedding at 35% drop when queue > 10k.
kevin: can we reroute some load to eu-west-1 or to a quantized variant? network egress and latency will bite for some clients though.
maria: quick triage options:
- short term: enable fallback to redwood-1-large-v2-8bit (quantized) for non-SLA customers + drop heavy batch sizes
- mid term: spillover routing to eu1 for 20% of traffic for this model
- alternative: throttle the top offending API keys via rate-limit policy
ops-oncall: I'm kicking off a scale action now (requesting +6 dedicated GPUs in usw2), ETA 6–9m for pods to be ready. will post when ready.
aj: if we scale, let's also lower batch_target from 128 -> 64 to reduce memory pressure and OOMs.
simon: agree on batch reduction. also enable KV cache warmup TTL extension — reduces compute on hot prefixes.
infra-bot: deploy-tool: submitted scale request: pool=usw2-large, delta=+6 gpus, change-id=deploy-20260118-0042
kevin: before we spill to eu1, check model variants there — eu1 only has quantized and small variants of redwood-1-large-v2. we can route non-SLA traffic to eu1-quant.
maria: i ran a quick dry command to inspect queues:
```
rictl queue list --region usw2 --model redwood-1-large-v2 --output json | jq '.queues | {depth: .depth, inflight: .inflight, drop_rate: .drop_rate}'
{
  "depth": 12345,
  "inflight": 3560,
  "drop_rate": 0.35
}
```
aj: also got a couple of stack traces showing "cudaMalloc failed" from two pods. suspect memory blowup from some requests with very long sequences.
ops-oncall: isolating pods with high OOMs and restarting. will mark them unschedulable if they keep crashing.
maria: can we temporarily enable request-size cap on API gateway? e.g., max_tokens=2048 for this model for next 1h.
kevin: we can. I'll push a temporary policy: "max_tokens=2048" + affix tag to identify customers we forced cap on.
simon: please do the following in parallel:
- aj: lower batch_target to 64
- kevin: enable fallback-to-quant for non-SLA route
- ops-oncall: scale +6 GPUs and quarantine crashing pods
- maria: toggle request-size cap and monitor drop-rate
aj: doing batch_target change now. patch in config pushed: `config-service set pool/usw2-large batch_target=64`
infra-bot: config-service: update accepted (change-id cfg-20260118-0123)
ops-oncall: scale request provisioned, nodes becoming ready (3/6 ready so far). watching pod autoscheduler. ETA full readiness ~8m.
maria: thanks. also let's prepare a mitigation note for CS — short explanation and ETA. will draft.
kevin: cost note — if we keep spillover to eu1 and scale in usw2, estimate incremental hourly cost +$1.2k. tag as emergency spend.
aj: batch change is live, memory OOMs reduced on first observation, inflight dropped to 2900, queue depth trending down (now ~9,100).
simon: good. keep an eye on p95 tail. if p95 stays >1.2s for 15m we should consider throttling specific API keys.
maria: drafting CS blurb now and adding list of top 10 API keys by request volume so sales knows who to call.
ops-oncall: all +6 GPUs ready, pods scheduled. early signals show queue depth dropping toward 4k.
maria: great — thanks team. we'll keep fallback routing enabled for 30m and re-evaluate. reopening postmortem if we see repeat.
kevin: after this stabilizes, let's run a capacity planning session: determine if we should pre-warm a small buffer for peak windows (SLO: keep drop_rate < 5%).
aj: noted. will collect traffic histograms and model sequence length distributions.
simon: one action item: add automated throttling rule that triggers when depth > 8k AND drop_rate > 20% to avoid manual ops next time.
maria: added to runbook items. will file ticket.
kevin: thanks all. I'll update cost tracker.
maria: CS note sent in #customer-success. monitoring.
ops-oncall: closing loop — queue depth 3,900, drop_rate 0.04, p95=780ms. marking incident mitigated at 09:33 UTC.
